questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Madison has some really interesting courses and professors in my field of study. The town of Madison is almost exclusively college students, I really wanted to be part of that kind of college experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It takes time but it's not that bad and when you're here all of that work is over.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance from the danish/american fellowship, scandesign. They have a storage unit filled with loaners items and bikes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There's a lot of international students and a lot of events for international students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think it's a lot easier in the spring semester. (most UW-students go on exchange in the spring semester because they want to be in Madison in the fall for football season). I used a Facebook group. Make sure not to pay before arrival though. Most Americans will be accommodating.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to live near campus! It makes it way more easy to be social all the time and to get home at night. I recommend the hub, The James and the embassy (or somewhere in this area).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Theres a lot of waiting for responses and a lot of making sure you know all of the deadlines. But after that you're all good.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I emailed different professors, course administrators and international advisers in the process and all responded with kindness.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was only one class that I didn't get - but I got another one that was interesting too. (I really recommend Film Comedy Com arts 300, if you happen to be studying film and media studies, or English).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the courses to be a lot easier but a lot more work.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A lot of small assignments during the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There's less of a direct connecting with the professors, but you have TA's for that). And there's designated office hours if you're interested.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CA300 film comedy , CA351 television industries, CA 325 media and human behavior , GEN&WS 101 introduction to gender and women's studies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend taking som gender and women's studies since that isn't possible at home. Film comedy was very cool and professional. The discussion sections was a really nice room to talk to other students.  
CA 325 was a bit disappointing. 

Also try and avoid friday classes. Thursday is thirsty Thursday.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travelling by plane within the United States is expensive. I knew that but I kind of forgot. I recommend book trips a bit in advance. I have spent most of money on social activities - I recommend saving up for this. I've travelled multiple times and done weekend trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fresh groceries are expensive. It's not necessarily cheaper than Denmark to go out and eat, but if you want something with fresh veggies it costs the same to make it at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend being part of the scan design foundation.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's so much sport. I played some badminton at the gym. The gym is easily the size of all Copenhagen fitness centers in one. There's a track on the top floor and an olympic swimming pool in the center.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Book a lodge up north and rent cars, go to Chicago, travel to New England for the weekend, take part in different student organized parties (eg. mifflin street block party). Watch sports! the college sport culture is insane!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Just talk to other students and exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I have two American roommates which is my no 1 tip.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans aren't as easy to make arrangements with - they're way more spontaneous than I find Danes to be.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All of my new friendships.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You're going to have so much fun - it will be worth all the hard work. 
2. be prepared to buy new clothes for this weird climate. 
3. Save up to have fuuuun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting to experience american (college) culture - good and bad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes you can be filled up with new impressions - it can be hard to say; ok, now I'll take a break and not experience anything the rest of the day.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
